ELECTION RESEARCH: 2026 B.C. provincial general election

Background for the roundup's election stories and any race the hosts mention. It is not the deep dive's subject. The Williams Lake Tribune school trustee results were not used for any race below.

**FINDINGS: Cariboo-Chilcotin**

On the ballot: Kathryn Askew (BC NDP), Lorne Doerkson (Conservative), Douglas Gook (BC Green). Seat held going in by Lorne Doerkson.

- **Kathryn Askew (BC NDP).** The 100 Mile Free Press (Oct. 1, 2026) reports she is a retired school teacher from Canim Lake and was named the NDP candidate for Cariboo-Chilcotin. The BC NDP release names her as the riding's candidate and says she has 32 years in education, including leadership roles with the BC Teachers' Federation and her local union (bcndp.ca, undated in the copy read). The same release says she was the NDP candidate for Mission-Matsqui-Abbotsford in the 2025 federal election. Her result in that race is not established: the Fraser Valley Current results page read carried no figures, and a pre-nomination Mission City Record piece names a different NDP candidate. Her 2026 campaign results: My Cariboo Now (Oct. 24, 2026, at time of writing) reports 3,123 votes, second place. Victoria News (Oct. 24, 2026) reports about 17.1 per cent with 75 of 89 ballot boxes counted. No controversy involving Askew was found.

- **Lorne Doerkson (Conservative).** Sourced background (Elections BC results, 2024-10-19): MLA for Cariboo-Chilcotin since 2020, first elected as a B.C. Liberal, re-elected in 2024 as a B.C. Conservative. BC Ballot (bcballot.ca, 2026 candidate page) gives his 2024 margin as 7,722 votes. Prior research, carried forward from Elections BC's 2020 statement of votes: 6,600 votes (51.25%) as a Liberal in 2020. Victoria News (Oct. 24, 2026) headlines his win as his "third time in a row" in the riding; the show has not established the details of the earlier election behind that headline. His 2026 result: My Cariboo Now (Oct. 24, 2026) reports 14,215 votes (77%) at time of writing; Victoria News (Oct. 24, 2026) reports 76.9% with 75 of 89 ballot boxes counted. The Globe and Mail (Sept. 26, 2026, carried forward) reports he took over as Conservative leader; Victoria News (Sept. 23, 2026, carried forward) reports he is interim leader.
  - *Campaign controversy (allegation, columnist's assessment, not a finding):* Vaughn Palmer's Vancouver Sun column (Oct. 7, 2026, carried forward; paywalled in the copy read) says Doerkson told reporters he had made "no promises at all" on auto insurance, and argues he had made four. Palmer writes that Doerkson twice denied making commitments of any kind. Doerkson's response, as reported in that column, is the denial.
  - *Related party matters (not about Doerkson personally):* The Tyee (Oct. 8, 2026, carried forward) reports he fired the party's Victoria-Beacon Hill candidate after social media posts the BC NDP flagged as racist. CityNews (Oct. 14, 2026, carried forward) reports a Conservative campaign director under fire over social posts will stay on, Doerkson says.

- **Douglas Gook (BC Green).** BC Green's candidate page (bcgreens.ca, 2026) lists him for Cariboo-Chilcotin and describes his forestry, reconciliation and environmental work. Elections BC's candidate report lists him for the riding. My Cariboo Now (Oct. 24, 2026) reports 1,103 votes at time of writing.
  - *Prior runs, as carried forward:* Caledonia Courier (Oct. 2024) reports he ran unsuccessfully four times as a Green candidate in North Cariboo, including a 2017 Nechako Lakes bid where he took about nine per cent. My Cariboo Now calls his 2020 bid his fourth run for the Greens in that riding. These two accounts do not reconcile the count of runs, and the show has not resolved it. Elections BC's 2020 statement of votes (carried forward) shows him at 707 votes (6.38%) in Cariboo North. CKPG Today (Sept. 13, 2024) announced him as the Green candidate for Nechako Lakes in 2024; his 2024 result is not established in the sources read.
  - No controversy was established.

**FINDINGS: Prince George-North Cariboo (includes Quesnel)**

On the ballot: Denice Bardua (BC NDP), Sheldon Clare (Conservative), Randy Thompson (BC Green). Seat held going in by Sheldon Clare. The Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 7, 2026) reports the three-candidate list was confirmed by Elections BC after nominations closed Oct. 3; CKPG Today (Oct. 3, 2026) lists the same three.

- **Denice Bardua (BC NDP).** CKPG Today (Sept. 24, 2024) reports she was announced as the NDP candidate in 2024. Her 2024 run: 3,426 votes, 17.0% (BC Ballot, Elections BC figures, 2024), finishing third behind Sheldon Clare and independent Coralee Oakes (4,394 votes, 21.8%). The Prince George Citizen (2026, undated in the copy read) also describes her as back on the ballot after a third-place finish with 17.03% in 2024. The earlier pass's "second place" description is incorrect: Oakes was second. The Prince George Citizen also describes her as an Indigenous education department secretary for School District 27. Her 2026 campaign result: the Prince George Citizen and My Cariboo Now (Oct. 24, 2026) carry the projected result; the Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 24, 2026) reports Clare projected to be re-elected. No controversy was established.

- **Sheldon Clare (Conservative, incumbent).** Sourced background (Elections BC results, 2024-10-19): won the riding for the B.C. Conservatives in 2024. Elections BC's 2024 statement of votes shows him at 11,430 votes, 56.82%. My Cariboo Now (Oct. 24, 2026) reports him declared MLA with over 10,000 votes, and the Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Oct. 24, 2026) reports him projected re-elected.
  - *Leadership bid (2026):* Times Colonist (Jan. 8, 2026, Canadian Press, carried forward) reports he said he was running for the B.C. Conservative leadership. CKPG Today (Jan. 20, 2026, carried forward) reports he formally launched the bid. CFJC Today (Feb. 28, 2026, carried forward) reports he suspended it, citing a leadership application issue in which some signatures were not accepted; he said he "takes full responsibility."
  - *Election-finance penalty (finding):* Elections BC's enforcement notice (March 30, 2026) and its April 1, 2026 release, as reported by CKPG Today (Apr. 1, 2026) and the Quesnel Cariboo Observer (Apr. 3, 2026), say he was fined $1,500 for accepting anonymous contributions for the 2024 election that exceeded the limit by about $4,000. Elections BC said the investigation found no deliberate attempt to circumvent the law. The Prince George Citizen reported the same penalty. His response to the penalty was not found in the sources read.
  - The prior pass's note on a September allegation was cut off in the copy received, so it is not carried forward here.

- **Randy Thompson (BC Green).** CKPG Today (Oct. 20, 2026) reports this is his second run for public office, the first being his 2024 bid for the same riding. He says he has served on the BC Green provincial council. The Prince George Daily News (Oct. 11, 2026) reports the party announced him as its candidate and says he is a farmer, small-business owner and municipal candidate; it also says he ran for the riding in the 2024 provincial election. His 2024 result: the Prince George Citizen (2026, undated in the copy read) reports 4.3% and fourth place; My Prince George Now (2024 live results) reports 848 votes (4.30%), last place. CKPG Today (Oct. 19, 2024) reports 790 votes (4.25%) on election night. No controversy was established. The CKPG Oct. 20, 2026 piece says Green candidates face harsh criticism on social media in general; that is his remark, not a specific incident.

NO RECORD FOUND: none
